title: Polymorphic TS SDK stream adapter: preserve backpressure & cancellation semantics
creator: Aisha Patel
description:
Problem: The TypeScript SDK supports both AsyncIterable (for Node/TS idiomatic consumers) and WHATWG ReadableStream/Web Streams (for browser/fetch/Deno). Today we have ad-hoc adapters that convert one form to the other, but they do not consistently preserve backpressure semantics, upstream cancellation propagation, or retry/resume behavior. This causes subtle bugs: partial responses getting lost on cancel, backpressure not applied to the underlying HTTP connection, and inconsistent behavior across environments (Node 18+, older Node, Deno, Bun).

Goal: Implement a polymorphic stream adapter layer that: (1) accepts/returns either AsyncIterable<T> or ReadableStream<T> depending on the consumer context; (2) preserves upstream pause/resume/backpressure so that large streaming responses do not overwhelm client memory or the network; (3) ensures cancellation by the consumer is propagated to the HTTP request/connection and to any runtime-specific stream resources; (4) provides clear retry semantics for transient failures with an optional resumable token protocol; (5) ships with ergonomic examples and tests for Node (streams+async iterators), browser fetch/Web Streams, and Deno.

Non-goals: Changing higher-level API shapes (we will keep the existing `client.stream()` surface). This ticket focuses on the adapter and reliability story, not on new user-facing method names.
acceptance_criteria: SDK exposes stable adapter that can be consumed as AsyncIterable or ReadableStream with identical event ordering and completion semantics
Canceling an AsyncIterator (via return() / throw()) or closing a ReadableStream will immediately signal the underlying fetch/request to abort and free resources
Backpressure from consumer limits read buffer and prevents unbounded memory growth for large token streams (>10MB payloads) in Node and browser tests
A documented retry/resume mechanism exists: for idempotent server-side resumable uploads we accept a resume token header and SDK will transparently retry when enabled
Cross-environment example snippets (Node, Browser, Deno) are added to the repo and documented in the SDK README
Automated E2E tests simulate slow consumers, mid-stream errors, and cancellation; CI shows deterministic behavior across Node 18/20 and a headless browser environment
implementation_notes: Introduce a small polymorphic layer `StreamBridge` that internally holds a single source-of-truth readable stream controller and exposes two facades: AsyncIterable<T> and ReadableStream<T>

Leverage AbortController/AbortSignal to wire consumer cancellation to fetch (node-fetch/fetch builtins). On Node we must ensure compatibility with native fetch AbortSignal behavior; include an adapter for libraries that use EventEmitter-style cancellation

Implement a bounded internal queue with configurable high/low water marks. When queue length > highWaterMark, pause underlying reader; when < lowWaterMark, resume. This provides backpressure to the producer loop without depending on environment-specific stream throttling alone

For AsyncIterable facade, implement the cancel path by calling controller.error() or controller.close() and invoking the AbortController; for ReadableStream facade, implement cancel() to call the same underlying abort

Retry behavior: expose `options.retry: { enabled: boolean, maxAttempts: number, resumableHeader?: string }`. On retryable transient errors, attempt to re-open the stream with the same request and pass a `resumption-token` header when server supports it. Retry only when request semantics are safe (e.g., generation streaming is idempotent or server-provided resume support exists)

Careful with UTF-8 chunk boundaries: adapters must not re-chunk text in a way that corrupts multibyte characters. Use a small buffer that concatenates bytes and emits only complete codepoints to consumer
Test matrix: Node 18, Node 20, Deno stable, Chromium headless (via Playwright) to assert behavior across runtimes
test_plan: Unit tests for StreamBridge internals: queue watermark transitions, error propagation, and cancellation hooks
Integration tests mocking fetch to stream payloads with variable production speed; assert that backpressure slows producer and memory stays within threshold
E2E cancel test: start consuming then call iterator.return() and assert that server received abort request and connections closed within 200ms
Retry/resume test: simulate transient network failure after N bytes, ensure SDK reopens stream and stitched payload equals original when resumable header is present
Cross-runtime smoke tests: run small script in Node 18, Deno, and Playwright browser that consumes via both AsyncIterator and Web Stream and verifies identical outputs
rollout: Feature flagged behind `ts_stream_polymorphic_adapter` for 2 weeks. Start with canary release to internal infra customers and SDK beta testers. Monitor memory/latency metrics and error rates in Console; rollback if consumer aborts are delayed >100ms or if retry leads to duplicated tokens in production during first 48h.

2026-03-05 - Elena Gomez (Reviews): Design looks good. Please document exact semantics for iterator.return() vs. iterator.throw() and how they map to readableStream.cancel(). Also note behavior for partial tokens delivered to user when cancellation occurs.

2026-03-10 - QA (Rohit Menon): Added test matrix for Node 18/20 and Playwright. Found race where abort sometimes doesn't close body stream on old node versions; added adapter fix to ensure body.cancel() is invoked when present.
